subject: Premium response SKU — accelerator credits & anchor discount terms
messages:

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Premium response SKU — accelerator credits & anchor discount terms

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Dedicated + Premium support yesterday. We're close to an internal green light but Procurement has two asks before we move to an amendment:

1) Can Redwood offer a staged discount if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool starting at $250k/month? We're looking for something north of 12.5% at full commit but would accept a step-up structure.
2) We need clarity on how premium credits apply during failover events — specifically whether accelerator credits are consumed before we hit SLA crediting.

I've attached our internal sizing and a simple worksheet with our anticipated usage. If you can propose a clean amendment that preserves our ability to use burst capacity in other regions that would be ideal.

Appreciate a quick sketch of options so our Procurement director (cc'd) can review this week.

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Head of Cloud Procurement
CloudVana
[Attachment: Pricing_Worksheet_CloudVana.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Premium response SKU — accelerator credits & anchor discount terms

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses below and attaching a compact SLA tier doc that maps credit consumption order:

- Discounting: We can do a stepped commit discount structure tied to a 12-month RX (reserved) spend. Example tiers: 0-$2.5M: base rate, $2.5M-$4.5M: 8% discount, $4.5M+: 14% discount. We can move the top end to 15% if CloudVana signs by Sept 10 and accepts a 60-day invoice cadence.

- Accelerator credits & failover: accelerator credits are applied to consumption for burst throughput first; SLA crediting (uptime-based) is calculated independently and then offset against future invoices. That means during a regional failover, burst = charged against credits; SLA credits are evaluated per SLA window and applied as separate invoice credits. See attached diagram.

Next steps: Ben (CC) will drop a pricing worksheet with the stepped commit table and Jordan will propose amendment language for procurement. I'll draft a short canary clause to preserve region-burst use.

I'll attach: SLA_Tiers_v3.pdf (maps crediting order) and a draft amendment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

[Attachment: Amendment_Draft.docx (docx)]

Subject: Re: Premium response SKU — accelerator credits & anchor discount terms

Elena — attaching a tabbed worksheet with three scenarios (Conservative, Expected, High-burst). Quick highlights:

- If CloudVana commits $3M ARR (12 months), the blended unit price falls ~10% from list.
- Moving to $5M ARR unlocks the 14% anchor step; the incremental savings are mostly on token unit price and on priority-lane fees.
- We can include a 90-day performance window: if usage ramps slower than modeled we hold the initial discount for the first quarter and true-up at month 4.

Callouts on credits: accelerator credits are billed as pre-paid consumption and drawdown in real-time. They are not automatically swept into SLA credits — we keep them separate to avoid double-crediting. SLA crediting is a contractual remedy applied after post-incident review.

If you want, Jordan and I can host a 30-min procurement-readout tomorrow at 11am PT and walk through the Excel.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
[Attachment: Pricing_Worksheet_CloudVana.xlsx (xlsx)]

Subject: Re: Premium response SKU — accelerator credits & anchor discount terms

Marissa, Ben — thanks, that helps a lot. Two follow-ups from Procurement after reviewing the worksheet:

1) The step-up to 14% is promising but Procurement is asking for a firm midpoint guarantee: if CloudVana hits 90% of the $5M threshold within 9 months, the 14% rate should retroactively apply to the earlier months (true-up). Is Redwood comfortable with a one-time true-up?
2) For audits we need an explicit clause that accelerator credits used in failover are visible in exported invoice line-items and in the Console. We want no ambiguity during our internal audit cycles.

We can do the DocuSign amendment if we can resolve those two items; Rajiv is prepared to move quickly if Jordan can supply the legal language for the true-up and the audit clause.

Best,
Elena

Elena / Rajiv — copying legal-sell-in language below for the two asks; happy to iterate. If these are acceptable we'll slot the amendment into DocuSign and route to you today.

1) True-up language (one-time retroactive adjustment):
"If Customer achieves >=90% of the committed 12-month reserved spend threshold of $5,000,000 within the first 270 days following the Effective Date, Redwood Inference will apply the tiered discount corresponding to the $5,000,000 threshold retroactively to charges incurred from the Effective Date through the date the threshold was met, in a one-time invoice credit."

2) Accelerator credits visibility (audit clause):
"All pre-paid accelerator credit consumption will be reflected as discrete line items on monthly invoices and made available via the Redwood Console export APIs (CSV/JSON) for the duration of the Agreement. During customer audits, Redwood will provide usage reports and exported billing line items for the relevant audit period."

If that wording looks good I can attach to the Amendment_Draft.docx and circulate the DocuSign link. We can accept standard redlines; only ask is that the true-up is limited to a single one-time credit to avoid ongoing retroactive churn.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Account Services
